a.summary: v1-live README still states every case funds its payer by airdrop and that the validator must serve the faucet
a.failure_scenario: "What the check covers" is the section a reader consults to decide whether the check can run anywhere; as written it says a faucet is mandatory, which is exactly the conclusion the new SAVA_V1_PAYER escape hatch exists to overturn. Someone landing on that section first will conclude a public-cluster run is impossible.

b.summary: README still states unconditionally that every case funds by airdrop, contradicting the new SAVA_V1_PAYER section
b.failure_scenario: This is the section a reader consults to learn what the check needs. Taken at face value it says the public-cluster path documented above it is impossible, since neither public faucet serves the check. The two statements cannot both be acted on, and the false one sits in the section that reads as the authoritative summary of requirements.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
